questions.stem: What happens to heart rate during exercise?

options.text: It stays the same
It decreases
It increases to deliver more oxygen and glucose to muscles
It stops temporarily

questions.explanation: Heart rate increases during exercise to pump blood faster, delivering more oxygen and glucose to working muscles and removing carbon dioxide and lactic acid more quickly.

questions.stem: Why does breathing rate increase during exercise?

options.text: To cool the body down
To take in more oxygen and remove more carbon dioxide to meet the increased demands of respiration
To reduce lactic acid in the lungs
To make the lungs bigger

questions.explanation: Breathing rate and depth increase to bring more oxygen into the blood for aerobic respiration in muscles and to remove the increased amounts of carbon dioxide produced.

questions.stem: What happens when muscles cannot get enough oxygen during intense exercise?

options.text: They start photosynthesising
They absorb oxygen from bones
They switch to anaerobic respiration, producing lactic acid
They stop working completely

questions.explanation: When oxygen supply cannot meet demand during intense exercise, muscles begin anaerobic respiration, producing lactic acid. This allows continued ATP production but causes fatigue.

questions.stem: How does the body remove lactic acid after exercise?

options.text: It is stored permanently in muscles
Blood transports it to the liver, where it is converted back to glucose or broken down with oxygen
It evaporates through the skin
It is excreted in urine immediately

questions.explanation: After exercise, lactic acid is transported by the blood to the liver, where it is converted back to glucose (or fully oxidised to CO2 and water using oxygen from the increased breathing rate).

questions.stem: Why do athletes have a higher stroke volume than non-athletes?

options.text: They have fewer red blood cells
They breathe less frequently
They have smaller hearts
Regular training strengthens the heart muscle, allowing it to pump more blood per beat

questions.explanation: Regular exercise strengthens the cardiac muscle, increasing the volume of blood pumped per heartbeat (stroke volume). This means the heart is more efficient and doesn't need to beat as fast.

questions.stem: What causes muscle fatigue during prolonged intense exercise?

options.text: Blood flow increases too much
Muscles run out of protein
Build-up of lactic acid, which lowers pH and interferes with enzyme function and muscle contraction
Too much oxygen in the muscles

questions.explanation: Lactic acid accumulation lowers the pH in muscles, which interferes with the enzymes needed for muscle contraction and causes pain and fatigue, eventually forcing the muscles to rest.

questions.stem: What changes occur in blood vessels supplying muscles during exercise?

options.text: They close completely
They move closer to the skin surface
They dilate (widen) to increase blood flow, delivering more oxygen and glucose
They narrow to reduce blood flow

questions.explanation: Blood vessels supplying active muscles vasodilate (widen) during exercise, increasing blood flow to deliver more oxygen and glucose and remove more waste products like CO2 and lactic acid.
